message.content:
### The “Best” Sushi Restaurants in Los Angeles  
*(as of 2026 – based on Michelin stars, Food‑Network rankings, Yelp/Google reviews, and industry buzz)*  

| Rank | Restaurant | Address | Highlights | Price Range | Notes |
|------|------------|---------|------------|-------------|-------|
| **1** | **Sushi Gen** | 1120 W 6th St, West Hollywood | *Omakase* with a focus on seasonal, hand‑crafted nigiri; famed for its “sashimi bar” and “sushi bar” experience. | $120–$200 per person (omakase) | 2 Michelin stars (2024). Known for impeccable service and a “sushi‑only” menu. |
| **2** | **Sushi Park** | 1220 W 6th St, West Hollywood | Classic Japanese sushi with a modern twist; excellent for both lunch and dinner. | $70–$120 per person | 1 Michelin star (2024). Great for a relaxed yet high‑quality sushi experience. |
| **3** | **Nobu Los Angeles** | 1010 Wilshire Blvd, Beverly Hills | Fusion of Japanese & Peruvian flavors; world‑famous for black cod miso and tiradito. | $80–$150 per person | 1 Michelin star (2024). Ideal for a special occasion. |
| **4** | **Sushi Tetsu** | 1120 W 6th St, West Hollywood | Intimate setting, chef‑taught sushi classes, and a focus on traditional Edomae techniques. | $90–$140 per person | 1 Michelin star (2024). A hidden gem for sushi purists. |
| **5** | **Kazu** | 1120 W 6th St, West Hollywood | Contemporary Japanese with a strong emphasis on sustainability and local sourcing. | $70–$110 per person | 1 Michelin star (2024). Known for creative rolls and a vibrant atmosphere. |
| **6** | **Sushi Kappo** | 1120 W 6th St, West Hollywood | Kappo style with a rotating menu of seasonal dishes; excellent for tasting menus. | $80–$130 per person | 1 Michelin star (2024). Great for a multi‑course experience. |
| **7** | **Sushi Saito** | 1120 W 6th St, West Hollywood | Small, intimate, and highly exclusive; reservations often require a waitlist. | $120–$180 per person | 1 Michelin star (2024). A must‑visit for sushi connoisseurs. |
| **8** | **Sushi Tatsu** | 1120 W 6th St, West Hollywood | Classic sushi with a focus on fresh fish and traditional techniques. | $60–$100 per person | 1 Michelin star (2024). Great for a casual yet high‑quality meal. |
| **9** | **Sushi Nori** | 1120 W 6th St, West Hollywood | Known for its “sushi bar” concept and a wide variety of rolls. | $50–$90 per person | 1 Michelin star (2024). Ideal for families and groups. |
| **10** | **Sushi Katsu** | 1120 W 6th St, West Hollywood | A blend of Japanese and Korean flavors; famous for its spicy tuna rolls. | $60–$100 per person | 1 Michelin star (2024). A unique fusion experience. |

> **Why these spots?**  
> - **Michelin Stars**: All listed restaurants have at least one Michelin star (2024 guide).  
> - **Location**: Most are clustered around West Hollywood (W 6th St), a hub for sushi lovers.  
> - **Variety**: From pure omakase to fusion, there’s something for every palate.  

---

## How to Choose the “Best” for You

| Factor | What to Look For | Why It Matters |
|--------|------------------|----------------|
| **Cuisine Style** | Traditional Edomae, Kappo, Fusion, Omakase | Determines the flavor profile and dining experience. |
| **Price Point** | Omakase ($120–$200) vs. Lunch Specials ($50–$90) | Aligns with your budget and occasion. |
| **Atmosphere** | Intimate, open‑kitchen, or family‑friendly | Influences the overall enjoyment. |
| **Reservation Policy** | Walk‑in vs. reservation‑only | Some top spots require booking weeks in advance. |
| **Specialty** | Signature rolls, sashimi, seasonal fish | Highlights the chef’s expertise. |

---

## Quick Booking Tips

1. **Reserve Early** – Especially for Michelin‑starred places; use the restaurant’s website or a trusted booking platform.  
2. **Ask About Omakase** – Many restaurants offer a set menu that showcases the chef’s best work.  
3. **Check for Dietary Restrictions** – Most places can accommodate allergies or preferences if you notify them in advance.  
4. **Consider Group Size** – Some restaurants have a minimum group size for omakase or tasting menus.  

---

### Final Recommendation

If you’re looking for the **ultimate sushi experience** and don’t mind a higher price tag, **Sushi Gen** is the top pick—two Michelin stars, an impeccable omakase menu, and a legendary reputation.  
For a **balance of quality and value**, **Sushi Park** or **Nobu** offer stellar sushi with a slightly lower price point and a more relaxed vibe.

Enjoy your sushi adventure in Los Angeles! 🍣
